content.title: The Savannah Bananas have unique rules. Here's what to know before they come to New Orleans.
content.text: Regularly playing in front of sold-out crowds, the Savannah Bananas have gained national popularity for their unique spin on baseball.The Bananas play a style of baseball known as “Banana Ball,” which aims to entertain fans with a fast-paced game involving tricks and stunts. The team is bringing its unique blend of baseball and in-game entertainment to New Orleans for the first time this weekend with a 6 p.m. game on Saturday and a 3 p.m. contest on Sunday at the Caesars Superdome. Listed below are the customized rules that make “Banana Ball” stand out compared to traditional baseball.Points win innings Teams score runs like in a traditional baseball game, but the highest-scoring team is awarded a point for scoring the most runs in an inning as opposed to each run counting toward the overall score. However, every run counts as a point in the game’s final inning. Savannah Bananas' Jared Donalson (21) dances on the field as the Savannah Bananas kick off the Baton Rouge portion of their world tour, Thursday, March 14, 2024, at Alex Box Stadium on the campus of LSU in Baton Rouge, La. STAFF PHOTO BY HILARY SCHEINUK Time limitEach game has a two-hour time limit, meaning no new innings can begin after two hours. Games can go nine innings like in traditional baseball, but the clock prevents a game from reaching that point if it’s at the two-hour mark. Batters can’t step outTo help with pace of play, batters can’t step out of the batter’s box while up to bat. If they do, it results in a called strike.Ejected for bunting Bunting is not allowed under any circumstances. If a batter bunts, they’re ejected from the game.Stealing firstA batter is allowed to steal first base while up to bat. Wild pitches and passed balls present opportunities.Sprints not walksA pitcher throwing ball four results in a sprint for the batter as opposed to a walk. The batter takes off running and can advance to as many bases as they can. The ball doesn’t become live until every defensive player on the field has touched it other than the pitcher and catcher. No mound visitsTo keep the pace up, no mound visits are allowed during the game from a coach or a position player. However, a team is allowed to hype their pitcher up from the dugout. Fan foul ball outA foul ball results in an out if a fan catches it.Tie breakerA “showdown tiebreaker” occurs if the game is tied after two hours. There are three showdown rounds, with a home run by either team resulting in a walk-off win. Each team will have the bases loaded with just one opposing fielder if still tied after three showdowns, and the first team to score wins. ChallengesEach team is allowed one on-field challenge per game. The three challenge categories include fair/foul ball calls, force/tag play calls and catches in the outfield or infield. However, a fan challenge is allowed once per game, with a designated fan holding up a sign to signal a challenge. Golden batterThe “golden batter” rule allows teams to send anyone they want up to bat once a game, allowing a team’s top hitter to come to the plate with the game on the line.Email Spencer Urquhart at surquhart@theadvocate.com.
